newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols erode as futures range - trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols erode as futures range - trade.

text.p: Bund options remained on the backfoot on Thursday as a restricted futures market ate away at implied volatility levels, traders said.
"We've seen sellers in every maturity month," said a trader at a German bank in Frankfurt. "At the moment people think there will be (futures) range-trading in the next couple of weeks."
He noted trade in par-102 strangles and said out-of-the- money puts had been sold on a directional basis as had out-of-the-money calls.
Adding to the downward pressure on volatility was a 10,000-contract sale of 100.50 calls on Wednesday, he said.
June volatility on June Bund futures was at 5.20-30 percent at early afternoon in Europe, he said. July, August and September all had mid-vol levels of around 5.40 percent.
The Frankfurt dealer said volatility had come down about 0.6 percentage point in the past two weeks.
A trader at a U.S. bank in London said debt markets looked pretty dull.
"There's no interest. We're waiting for the G7 meeting this weekend," he said. "Currencies and the stock markets are the the focal points at the moment."
The trader said the 101.00-101.50 region could be an area where some people would want to put on put options.
June Bunds at 1310 GMT were at 100.94, up 0.13 on the day. Since a sharp gain on April 15 they have stayed in a less-than-one-point band between 100.35 and 101.14.

In slightly broader terms, the Bund futures market has been gradually trending upwards since a 99.05 low on April 3. But the U.S. bank trader said that while some banks have been buying futures lately, there are plenty out there who are quickly hedging those positions with puts.
"Everybody's kind of looking over their shoulder," he said.
